--- title: prefetch nav_title: prefetch description: Defer runtime work until a per-link prefetch or navigation with the prefetch function. related: links: - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching - app/guides/keeping-pages-static - app/api-reference/functions/navigation - app/api-reference/functions/connection - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching --- Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell. Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output. ## Usage The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5} import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` With Partial Prefetching enabled, Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages): 1. A default `` loads the App Shell, which holds the part of the route that does not depend on the URL. 2. An optional [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or [`router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), can also load content that depends on the link's URL. 3. When the user follows the link, the navigation renders the rest of the route. During runtime rendering, awaiting `prefetch()` keeps content out of the App Shell, so it renders during a per-link prefetch or navigation. Static prerenders can still include the content. Calling `router.prefetch(href)` without `kind: 'full'` requests only the App Shell under Partial Prefetching. It does not render content below `await prefetch()`. To keep content out of per-link prefetches as well, so it renders only on the navigation, use [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation). > **Good to know**: `prefetch()` defers one subtree. To require a static App Shell across the route, use [`ensureStatic = 'shell'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic#shell). See [Keeping pages static](/docs/app/guides/keeping-pages-static) for a worked example. Everything above `prefetch()` renders in the App Shell, and everything below renders on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. Deferral is scoped to the component that awaits it and the tree below: sibling branches render in the shell as usual. Place it above the work to defer, and wrap the component in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense): ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" highlight={25} switcher import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { cacheLife, prefetch } from 'next/cache' export default function Page() { return ( <> Loading greeting...

}> {/* in the App Shell */} Loading recommendations...

}> {/* the fallback is in the App Shell, the recommendations are not */} ) } async function Greeting() { const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return

{session ? 'Welcome back' : 'Welcome'}

} async function Recommendations() { await prefetch() // runtime work below renders on a per-link prefetch or navigation const items = await getRecommendations() return } async function getRecommendations() { 'use cache: private' cacheLife('hours') const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return db.recommendations.rank({ session }) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" highlight={25} switcher import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { cacheLife, prefetch } from 'next/cache' export default function Page() { return ( <> Loading greeting...

}> {/* in the App Shell */} Loading recommendations...

}> {/* the fallback is in the App Shell, the recommendations are not */} ) } async function Greeting() { const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return

{session ? 'Welcome back' : 'Welcome'}

} async function Recommendations() { await prefetch() // runtime work below renders on a per-link prefetch or navigation const items = await getRecommendations() return } async function getRecommendations() { 'use cache: private' cacheLife('hours') const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return db.recommendations.rank({ session }) } ``` The greeting reads the session and stays in the App Shell. The recommendations read it too, inside `getRecommendations`, so that read is deferred along with the ranking. Remove `prefetch()` and they become part of the App Shell that every link into the route loads. Put the directive on a function called below it, as `getRecommendations` does here. Awaiting `prefetch()` inside a cached scope, such as [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), is not allowed. ## How `prefetch()` differs from `connection()` The [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function waits for a real request. It excludes the code that follows from prerendering and prefetching, making that work request-dependent. Awaiting `prefetch()` excludes the code that follows from the App Shell. It can resolve during a per-link prefetch without making that work request-dependent. A function called after `await prefetch()` can therefore use [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and keep its cache lifetime without generating its result for every link into the route. Use `connection()` when the work must run for a real request. Use `prefetch()` when the work is reusable but should only run for a selected per-link prefetch or a navigation. ## When to use it Use `prefetch()` when the content below it is expensive to produce and should not be generated in the App Shell that every `` into the route loads. Producing the App Shell does not run that code, so its upstream requests are not issued until a per-link prefetch or the navigation. Leaving content uncached also keeps it out of the shell, but gives up its cache lifetime and cannot make it available during a per-link prefetch. With `prefetch()`, the content can be cached with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), given a lifetime, and deferred to a per-link prefetch or navigation. Uncached reads, values with a short [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time, and anything behind `params` or `searchParams` are already left out of the shell on their own. ### Keeping the App Shell static When every read of [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) and [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) sits below `prefetch()`, the prerender a shell prefetch would trigger cannot produce more than the static output the build already generated, so the shell is served from that output instead. Shaping a route this way is an optional optimization: a static response can be cached in a CDN, so a default `` into the route costs no server CPU at all. A route that resolves `params` or `searchParams` gets that prerender instead, and so does the example above: its greeting reads the session in the shell, so the shell renders once per visitor and only the recommendations are deferred. ## Good to know - The function has no effect on the initial load of a page. - Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), it does not mark the subtree as request-dependent. Content below `await prefetch()` stays fully cacheable and can be wrapped in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). - A call outside a `` boundary surfaces an [Instant Insight](/docs/messages/instant-navigation-stage) in development. A fully prerendered route is unaffected, but the insight identifies that the call would defer content without a fallback if the route later requires runtime rendering. - Calling it inside `use cache`, `use cache: private`, [`unstable_cache()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache), [`after()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after), [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params), or a Client Component throws. - In a `page` or `layout` that sets the [`prefetch` route segment config](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch), import the function under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, since both are named `prefetch`. ## Reference ### Type ```ts function prefetch(): Promise ``` ### Parameters - The function does not accept any parameters. ### Returns A `Promise`. It is not meant to be consumed. ## Version History | Version | Changes | | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `v16.4.0` | `prefetch` introduced, replacing the `unstable_prefetch` name used in earlier canary releases. | - [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) defers the code until a per-link prefetch or navigation. - [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) defers the code until navigation. In the following diagram, a gray dashed outline marks the Suspense fallback, while blue marks the deferred work once it renders: Both functions apply only during runtime rendering, so they do not change a fully static route. Each call defers the component that awaits it and that component's descendants. Earlier stages render the nearest [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) fallback, which the deferred subtree replaces when its stage runs. Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), neither function makes the subtree request-dependent, so functions within it can still use `use cache`. See [How `navigation()` differs from `connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation#how-navigation-differs-from-connection). ### Keep expensive session data out of the App Shell Take the dashboard again. A ranking keyed on the session is expensive, and every default `` into the dashboard would generate it for the shell. Await `prefetch()` above the ranking so that only a `` resolves it before the click: ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/recommendations.tsx" highlight={6} import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { prefetch } from 'next/cache' async function Recommendations() { const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value await prefetch() const items = await rank(session) return } async function rank(session?: string) { 'use cache: private' return db.recommendations.rank({ session }) } ``` The session is read above `prefetch()`, so it still resolves in the shell. The App Shell does not generate the ranking. A default `` includes the `` fallback, which the ranking replaces during navigation. A `` resolves the ranking before the click. `rank` keeps its cache lifetime in both cases. Neither function can be awaited inside a cached scope, so the directive goes on a function called below it, as `rank` does here. ### Wait for the navigation Consider an inbox where each visible thread uses ``. The prefetch should include the thread subject, but fetching every message body before the user opens it would waste work. Render the latest message in its own `` boundary and await `navigation()` before loading it: ```tsx filename="app/inbox/[threadId]/thread.tsx" highlight={19} import { Suspense } from 'react' import { navigation } from 'next/cache' import { getLatestMessage, getThreadSummary } from '@/lib/mail' export async function Thread({ threadId }: { threadId: string }) { const thread = await getThreadSummary(threadId) return (

--- title: prefetch nav_title: prefetch config description: Configure how a route segment is prefetched during client navigation. related: title: Next Steps description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice. links: - app/guides/instant-navigation - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant --- The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below. > **Good to know**: > > - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. > - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component. > - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly. > - A `page` or `layout` that also calls the [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) function needs to import it under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`. ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher export const prefetch = 'partial' export default function Page() { return
...
} ``` ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher export const prefetch = 'partial' export default function Page() { return
...
} ``` ## Options ### `'partial'` Opts the segment into [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) without enabling the global [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag. A `` pointing at a segment with `prefetch = 'partial'` loads the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) instead of the legacy full prefetch. Set this on the destination, not the link. For links that opt into a wider prefetch with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), Next.js uses per-link prefetching. The server renders a fresh response that resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL). On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache. If a page accesses non-static data, it's prefetched at runtime. Use this for incremental adoption when you can't enable `partialPrefetching` for the entire app at once. Once every route in scope has `prefetch = 'partial'`, enable the global flag and remove the per-route exports. > **Good to know**: When Next.js performs a per-link prefetch for a segment, all downstream segments are included in the same request. Segments deeper in the tree that are configured with `'force-disabled'` will still be prefetched as part of the response. ```tsx filename="page.tsx" export const prefetch = 'partial' ``` ### `'force-disabled'` Never prefetch this segment. The client will not request segment data ahead of navigation. Use this for segments where prefetching would be wasteful, for example pages behind authentication that are rarely visited. > **Good to know**: `'force-disabled'` does not prevent Next.js from prefetching metadata about the route. However, the actual segment data for this segment and all deeper segments will be omitted from prefetching. ## Relationship with the `` prop A prefetch starts with a `` that expresses intent (should this destination be prefetched, and how eagerly), and ends at a segment that sets a cost ceiling (how much work is it OK to do ahead of time, for any link that points here). item.text: Next’s cache API has a staging hook for this exact split: a default link prefetch can stop at the product-page shell, while an explicitly eager link can resolve the deferred content. I’m using that around the related-products section and making the featured link eager.

Default product-page prefetches now stop at the page shell; the related-products section is deferred behind a Suspense boundary and `prefetch()` in [app/product/page.tsx](/workspace/app/product/page.tsx:5). The featured-product link opts into full prefetch, so related products can be ready before navigation in [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx:7).

I didn’t run tests. There are also existing changes to `package.json` and `package-lock.json` in the worktree; I left them untouched.
